name: Textarea
summary: Lets people enter or edit several lines of text.
description: A textarea collects free text that may run over several lines: a message, a description, a comment, an address. It shows a chosen number of lines, scrolls beyond them and can be resized. It has a visible label above, an optional description and, when its value fails validation, a message under it. One line of text is a Text field.

anatomy.description: Root. Stacks the label, the control, the description and the message; carries the size and the forced state.
Text naming the field. Provides the accessible name; activating it focuses the control.
The editable box: the native multi-line text control, drawn by the component. Receives focus, holds the value, shows the placeholder while empty and as many lines as the rows property.
Optional help text under the control (format, example, consequence), associated with it as its description.
Text saying what the severity means (what is wrong and how to fix it, what to check, what was confirmed), associated with the control as a description. Shown only with a severity.

properties.name: Size
properties.description: Control height, inline padding and text size scale together; label, description and message keep their size.

options.description: Dense forms, toolbars, table rows (32 px high).
Prominent, single fields: a search page, a sign-in form (48 px).

properties.name: Label
properties.description: What the field asks for, as a noun phrase (Email address). Always visible.

properties.name: Placeholder
properties.description: Short hint shown while the field is empty, in a lighter color. It disappears when people type: never the label, never an instruction people must remember.

properties.name: Rows
properties.description: Number of text lines visible before the control scrolls; people can resize it vertically.

properties.name: Description
properties.description: Help text: expected format, example, or what the value is used for.

properties.name: Message
properties.description: What the severity means: what is wrong and how to fix it, what to check, or what was confirmed. Shown with a severity, in the color of that severity, and replaces errorMessage.

properties.name: Required
properties.description: The field must be filled to submit the form.

properties.name: Read-only
properties.description: The value can be read, focused and copied but not edited (a generated identifier).

properties.name: Severity
properties.description: What the check of the value found. Replaces the invalid boolean: error, warning and success are the three severities of a form control (decision forms-severity); information that holds before any check is the description's job.

options.description: No severity: nothing was checked, or there is nothing to say (default).
The value is not accepted: the border takes the error color, the message says what is wrong and how to fix it, and the control is exposed as in error (aria-invalid on the web).
The value is accepted but deserves attention: the border takes the warning color and the message says what to check. No web state: said in the message text.
The value was checked and confirmed: the border takes the success color and the message says what was confirmed. No web state: said in the message text.

properties.name: Disabled
properties.description: Non-interactive and skipped by the keyboard; the value stays visible. Prefer read-only when people may need to read or copy the value.

states.description: Resting: an outlined box on the default surface.
Pointer over the control. The box takes the surface hover tint; the border does not change. Needs a pointing device: touch has no hover.
Focus on the control, from the keyboard or a pointer: an editable field shows the shared focus ring outside its border however it was focused.
Severity error: the border takes the error color and the message is shown under the control, in the error color.
Severity warning: the border takes the warning color and the message is shown under the control, in the warning color. No web state beyond the data attribute.
Severity success: the border takes the success color and the message is shown under the control, in the success color. No web state beyond the data attribute.
Not editable: the box takes the level 1 surface; the value stays focusable and selectable.
Non-interactive. Box, value, label and description drop to the shared disabled colors; hover and focus do not apply.

notes: Label, control, description and message stack, separated by container.gap; the control fills the width of the component, which the layout sizes.
Inline padding, minimum height and text size come from the size option; the corner radius and the border width do not change.
The block padding sets the inset of the first and last lines; the control grows with the rows property and can be resized vertically.

name.text: Computed from the label, associated with the control as its label element on the web. The description and the message are exposed as the accessible description, not as part of the name. The placeholder is exposed as a placeholder and used as a name only when nothing else names the control, which never happens here.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to the control. A disabled control is not focusable and is skipped.

guidelines.text: Expose the textbox role, the name, the value and the required, read-only, disabled and error states through the platform's native multi-line text control, so assistive technology receives them without extra work.
Use the native textarea element: it exposes the textbox role as multi-line, with its value and states, without ARIA.
Every field has a visible label associated with the control programmatically; help text that people need to fill the field (format, example) is visible too, as the description.
Associate the label with a label element whose for attribute names the control's id; reference the description and the message with aria-describedby, so they are read after the name.
The placeholder is a short hint, never the label and never an instruction: it disappears as soon as people type, and is not exposed as the name when a label exists.
Show a hint in a text field to help communicate its purpose; because placeholder text disappears when people start typing, include a separate label describing the field.

Say the severity in text next to the field, whatever it is: the message names what is wrong and how to fix it for an error, what to check for a warning and what was confirmed for a success, and is associated with the control. Color is never the only sign of a severity.

Say that the value is in error with aria-invalid="true" on the control, for the error severity only, and that a field is required with the required attribute, which the browser exposes as required. The web has no state for a warning or a success: the message says them, and aria-invalid is never set for them.
Mark required fields in the label or the description, never by the error color alone.

Label, value, description and message text contrast at least 4.5:1 with their background in every color mode and enabled state: label and value 19.03:1 (light) and 11.28:1 (dark) on the default surface, description 12.78:1 and 8.86:1, placeholder 6.08:1 and 6.40:1, message text in its severity color: error 6.12:1 and 7.06:1, warning 13.01:1 and 11.17:1, success 7.87:1 and 7.89:1 (on every surface level the lowest are error 5.79:1 in light mode and 5.30:1 in dark mode, warning 12.30:1 and 8.38:1, success 7.44:1 and 5.92:1). Disabled text is inactive and exempt.

The border is what identifies the field, so it contrasts at least 3:1 with the adjacent surface in every color mode: 12.78:1 (light) and 11.28:1 (dark) on the default surface at rest, 12.09:1 and 10.33:1 on the hover tint; the severity borders (the accent functional border): error 6.12:1 and 4.97:1, warning 3.27:1 and 8.09:1, success 7.87:1 and 6.08:1 on the default surface, and at least 5.79:1 and 3.73:1 (error), 3.09:1 and 6.07:1 (warning), 7.44:1 and 4.57:1 (success) on every surface level; the focus ring 5.77:1 and 12.76:1. Disabled is exempt. A warning border on the subtle warning fill, which a field may take as its fill in step 6, is 2.95:1 in light mode: a known shortfall (issue #119).
A visible focus indicator appears when the control receives focus, drawn outside its border.
The focus ring is drawn with :focus-visible, which browsers match whenever an editable field has focus, pointer or keyboard.
Every size is a pointer target of at least 24 x 24 CSS pixels through its minimum height: 32, 40 and 48 pixels.

Fields that collect information about the person (name, email, phone, address) carry the matching autocomplete token, so browsers and assistive technology can identify their purpose. The template passes it through its extra attributes.
A read-only field keeps its value focusable and selectable and is exposed as read-only; a disabled field leaves the focus order. Prefer read-only when people may need to read or copy the value.
Apple recommends a hit region of at least 44 x 44 pt; the small and medium sizes (32 and 40 pt) fall under it on iOS today: the Figma library has no platform heights.

Android recommends a touch target of at least 48 x 48 dp; the small and medium sizes (32 and 40 dp) fall under it on Android today. Expose an error with the error semantics so the message is announced with the field.
Color transitions of the control are removed when the user asks for reduced motion.

guidelines: The label is a noun phrase naming the information asked for: Message, Description, Delivery notes. Sentence case, no colon, no trailing punctuation.
The description says what to include, or a length limit, when it helps: Up to 500 characters.
The placeholder, when any, is a short example, never an instruction and never the label.
The message of an error says what is wrong and how to fix it: Enter a message of at least 20 characters.

decisions.text: The Textarea always renders the same box as the Text field of the same size and state: height, inline padding, text, border, corners, colors, focus ring, label, description, message and motion are the Text field's, and only its block padding and its rows are its own. A Text field decision on any of these applies to the Textarea in the same change: pnpm validate fails when a Textarea token differs from the Text field token at the same place (MIRRORS in scripts/lib/mirrors.mjs, decision field-family-mirrors of the Text field). The mirror covers rendering only: a contract decision is asked for the Textarea too.
decisions.rationale: Nothing tied the three plain fields to the Text field: a decision on its box left them behind. Mirroring them lets every rendering step of the Text field refinement change the four in the same commit, and pnpm validate prove they agree, where the alternatives (the Text field alone, with a closing step per sibling or an issue for the others) leave the siblings out of step in between. The Select is not mirrored now: it gets its own step later, with the complex controls.

decisions.text: The control shows one of three severities, set by the severity property (none by default, error, warning, success): its border takes the severity's accent functional border color and the message, the message property shown only with a severity, takes the severity's functional text color. A message carries every severity, in the same part; severity replaces the invalid property and message replaces errorMessage. On the web the error is aria-invalid="true" (and :user-invalid when the browser validates) and the severity is also data-severity; warning and success have no web state and are said in the message text. The fill, the icon and the message wording of each severity are rendered in Forms step 6. The accent borders reach 3:1 on every surface level since the Color foundation 7.1.0 (decision border-accent-functional-3-to-1); the light warning border is 2.95:1 on the subtle warning fill, which step 6 may use as the fill, a shortfall the team accepted knowingly (issue #119).
decisions.rationale: The team validated the Forms foundation's three severities (decision forms-validation-severities) and named the property severity; "error" is the word every platform uses (WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification, Compose error semantics, Material error text), where "invalid" is the web's technical term. The clean break is deliberate: the packages are alpha and unreleased, and a deprecated alias would cost a schema field and support in the validator, the bridge and the templates. This amends decisions field-colors and label-description-error, whose text still says invalid and error message.

decisions.text: The control is a box on the default surface outlined in the accent neutral border color; hover tints it with the surface hover color and keeps the border; invalid takes the base error border; read-only takes the level 1 surface; disabled takes the shared disabled colors. Value text is primary, the placeholder tertiary, the description secondary, the error message the error text color.
decisions.rationale: The Figma library maps no color to form controls. The accent neutral border is the lightest neutral border that keeps 3:1 against the surface in both modes (WCAG 1.4.11); the hover tint reuses the surface's own hover step.

decisions.text: Three sizes from the Figma library's space and body scales: small (32 px high, 8 px inline padding, 14 px text), medium (40, 12, 16, the default) and large (48, 16, 20); the border is 0.6 px (stroke-width.sm) and the corners 4 px (corner-radius.xs) at every size; label, description and error message keep 14 px.

A field always has a visible label above the control; help text goes under the control as the description, and the error message under it while the field is invalid. Both are exposed as the control's description.
The textarea shows the number of lines of its rows property (three by default), with a block padding of 6, 8 or 12 px by size, and people can resize it vertically; it never resizes horizontally.

changelog.note: Decision same-box-as-text-field (Text field decision field-family-mirrors): the Textarea is a mirror of the Text field, so every Text field decision on the box applies here in the same change and pnpm validate compares the tokens; its block padding is declared as its own. No token, CSS or template change: the tokens already resolve to the Text field's values in every platform and mode, so sizes, colors and contrast are unchanged.

Breaking, decision forms-severity: the invalid property is replaced by severity (none, error, warning, success), errorMessage by message and the part error-message by message, the state invalid by error, warning and success; the web attribute data-invalid by data-severity. Tokens: control.border-color.invalid is control.border-color.error, with warning and success and reads the accent functional border (global.border.accent.functional.<severity>.default) instead of the base error border; error-message.* is message.*, and message.color.<severity> reads global.text.on-base.functional.<severity>.default. CSS: [data-severity="<severity>"] and [data-state="<severity>"], textarea__error-message is textarea__message. The accent borders reach 3:1 on every surface level since the Color foundation 7.1.0 (decision border-accent-functional-3-to-1); the light warning border is 2.95:1 on the subtle warning fill, which step 6 may use as the fill, a shortfall the team accepted knowingly (issue #119).

Fix, no decision changed: the Figma library's POC2 export (Color foundation 3.1.0) moves the values of the roles the tokens alias; the tokens, CSS and template are unchanged. Light: 8 tokens follow the ash retune (one to four units per channel); error-message.color reads global.text.on-base.functional.error.default: #E12A23 becomes #C01619. Dark: 8 tokens follow the ash retune (one to four units per channel); control.border-color.default reads global.border.accent.neutral.default: #B9B7B7 becomes #CFCFCF; control.border-color.invalid reads global.border.base.functional.error.default: #E12A23 becomes #DF2821; error-message.color reads global.text.on-base.functional.error.default: #EE5248 becomes #F88275. Contrast re-measured on the accessibility guidelines: 3.82 → 3.73:1, 4.26 → 5.79:1, 4.52 → 6.12:1, 4.97 → 7.06:1, 5.79 → 5.77:1, 6.36 → 6.40:1, 11.27 → 11.28:1, 12.14 → 12.09:1, 12.80 → 12.76:1, 12.87 → 12.78:1, 19.07 → 19.03:1.

Initial draft (decisions field-colors, sizes, label-description-error, rows-and-resize). Native textarea in a wrapper with a label element, a description and an error message; states default, hover, focus-visible, invalid, readonly, disabled; sizes small, medium, large. Contrast on the default surface, light / dark: label and value 19.07 / 11.27, description 12.87 / 8.80, placeholder 6.08 / 6.36, error text 4.52 / 4.97 (4.26 on level 1 in light mode), border at rest 12.87 / 8.80 and 12.14 / 8.06 on hover, error border 6.12 / 3.82, focus ring 5.79 / 12.80.
